SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 08/31/2020
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 893141
Permit API: 125-28618
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Robinson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 08/31/2020
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 8/30/2020 at approximately 3:30 PM. According to the operator, due to human error a shut valve was left open which allowed reuse water to travel from the tank pad to the well pad storage tanks which then over flowed into secondary containment. An additional amount appeared to splash off into the R3 riprap adjacent to the secondary containment. SPSI was dispatched to remediate the off containment spill and a vacuum truck was already on site to remove what was lost to secondary containment.According to the operator 1,043 gallons was removed from secondary containment. 5-7 gallons is reported to have been lost off containment.On my arrival I was met by operator representative Brandon Carson and Jason Dockum Water Supervisor. The site is actively being frac'd, but is down for an inspection. SPSI is not on site, the operator reports that remediation efforts have been completed and a single roll off box is awaiting pick up (Photo 10).The ERP is on site in the mailbox. Safety Data Sheets are located in the trailer along with the secondary containment log (Photo 9). The secondary containment was inspected on both 8/30 and 8/31. No leaks to containment were reported and no visible leaks are currently observed.There is still a rust colored fluid in secondary containment (Photo 2). According to the operator, the mats are being washed off and a vac truck is on site to remove the water. The operator reports that this is not from the spill incident.The operator reports that the over flow was observed immediately and the shut in valve to the storm drain was closed (Photo 4). No sheen is observed in the drain or at the PCSM feature (Photo 6, 7, & 8).The operator reports that the valve will be closed until the next rain to verify everything was adequately cleaned.Visually impacted material appears to have been remediated (Photo 1, 3, & 5). The visually remediated area was probed for conductivity, nothing over .5 Sm was detected.The Department requests that the waste manifest be submitted to the Department as soon as possible.Based on this inspection violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending receipt of the waste manifest, and further investigation, more violations may be issued.

properties.content:

Violation ID: 8201224
Permit API: 129-27237
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Mount Pleasant Borough
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/13/2024
Comments: On 9/13/24 OGI Chuck Reaggle accompanied WQS Tori LaBirt and PGM Matthew Dracup to perform a complaint related O and G inspection of the FRICK PARK 1 OG well. Permit number# 129-27237 related to complaint number-383365. At the time of inspection: 1. Well appears to be active and producing. 2. 2023 Annual production report and 2023 Mechanical integrity assessment have been submitted. 3. Small gas leaks were detected at the connections downstream from the dump valve on the separator(suggesting that the dump valve isn't holding as well) and small detection of gas from the open annulus. 4. No spills observed. 5. No leaks observed from the brine tank. 6. Light corrosion observed. 7. Well tag attached to the well. 8. Operator posting with address, phone number, well name, well permit number. 9. Field supervisor met with us on site to allow full access to inspect. Violations issued as result of this inspection: 78.74 - Venting of gas. Recommendations: 1. Correcting the leaks involving the dump valve/connections below the dump valve. 2. Closing and/or monitoring the annulus, and routing the annulus vent up from ground level to above 6-7'. 3. Painting / rust prevention to slow corrosion, as some time before any corrosion level result in a leak issue. 4. Inform OGI Chuck Reaggle when all leaks are corrected so a follow up inspection can be conducted.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 8/01/2023 to ALLSHOUSE TERRENCE L JR in Pleasant Township, Warren county. OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ALLSHOUSE TERRENCE L JR
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 8/01/2023
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 8154392
Permit API: 123-42070
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/01/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. All valves were open and the well is currently equipped for production. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. The operator had this well improperly labeled with the wrong API# and the issue was promptly addressed. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation. 2% Methane was detected in slam bar holes #2 and #3 utilizing a MSA ALTAIR 5X Meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023, however the methane quickly dissipated and no sample was attainable. At this time due to the low methane readings and the readings dissipating quickly the department will continue to monitor this well for methane outside of the casing. Future inspections may warrant violations. An investigation as to the possible source of methane should be conducted by the operator.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia's Crain well site located in Rome Township, Bradford County on 10/6/2023 at 1025 hours. The weather was 67 degrees with cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Chesapeake. Complaint tracking system (CTS) ID # 375421 is tied to this release within CTS.Chesapeake reported that on 10/5/2023 at 1030 hours, a release of approximately 150 gallons of methanol was spilled to the pad surface when its storage container was being moved with a forklift. Chesapeake reported that a water truck was utilized to recover all of the standing fluid on the pad surface and the impacted area was excavated. All impacted pad material was placed in waste containers and covered. Chesapeake reported that no portion of the release was able to runoff the site. Chesapeake confirmed that the clean-up was completed on 10/5/2023 and had an environmental consultant respond to collect soil characterization samples. During my inspection, there was no evidence observed indicating that the release was not properly remediated. Based on the reported release of ~150 gallons of methanol, violations of the following are cited against API # 015-23853 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)I departed the site at 1100 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/15/2025
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8241171
Permit API: 015-23892
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/15/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) well site located in Troy, Springfield and Columbia Townships, Bradford County on 7/15/2025 at 1000 hours. The weather was around 80 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. A discussion with Repsol representatives indicated the following: The first plug on the 7H well was successfully set on 7/14/2025 at ~2100 hours. The flow of fluids from the well stopped after the first plug was set but "surging" was reported which was still causing fluids to reach the pad surface. A second plug was successfully set at ~0500 hours on 7/15/2025 which stopped all flow of fluids from the well. A third, precautionary plug was scheduled to be set on 7/15/2025. During the DEP's inspection, it was noted that a significant amount of the fluids that were pooled on the pad surface and within the pad-wide secondary containment have since been recovered or have flowed off of the pad surface. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed within the constructed "corner" berm (photo #4), the secondary berm/trench (photo #5), and the stormwater control basin (photos #7 and 8). The tertiary berm that was constructed as a precaution in the event of a rain event (photo #6) was observed to be dry today. The DEP continued creating/screening monitoring points around the pad, the stormwater control basin and downslope of the pad. Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were noted downslope of the western corner of the well pad, below the constructed "corner" berm, which were also noted on 7/14/2025.The under-drain outlet pipe for the post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) basin was plugged on 7/14/2025. Repsol observed that the plug was still dripping fluids so a secondary seal was placed over the outlet (photo #9).Resource Environmental (Resource) began evaluating potentially impacted areas onsite to determine the extent of the surface impacts of the release, including surface soils screening. Resource conducted drone flights to take high resolution overview photos of the site in order to produce a detailed map summarizing the screening points/data.As per the DEP recommendations on 7/14/2025, a wash station for cleaning of trucks prior to site departure was installed in the evening hours on 7/14/2025. The wash station can be seen in photo #1.As per 25 Pa. Code 78a.66b(4), Moody and Associates continued the sampling/screening of nearby water supplies on 7/15/2025.Violations of the following remain outstanding against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, Clean Streams Law 401, and SWMA 301.The DEP recommends the following:-continuing the evaluation of impacted areas and executing a plan to prevent additional environmental impacts-covering impacted areas to prevent precipitation from saturating the soils-installing erosion and sediment control best management practices downslope of the exposed soil areas to prevent accelerated erosion/sedimentation from escaping the site-continuing fluid recovery The DEP departed the site at 1145 hours. For information regarding the DEP's inspection from 7/14/2025, please see inspection record #4012602.

Comments: On 03/27/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the Anthony Petraitis Well Site following receipt of a spill report, submitted to the Department on 03/26/2026 (CTS 396174). I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Laura Grada (PA DEP), EQT representative Doug Oberdorf, and SPSI representative Billy Wade. SPSI was on site for remediation.EQT reported a spill of approximately 5 gallons of production fluid from a flow line. They reported that SPSI was on site, the release was contained, and no waterways were affected.EQT indicated on site that they intend to remediate per Act 2 guidelines. The fluid was on the pad, underneath the pad liner; the pad liner was above the pad substrate and contained pea gravel overtop of the liner. When the Department arrived on site, SPSI indicated that 1 vac box was around half full of the removed fluids; this was the only box that was used, and none were removed from site full.The following was observed during inspection:SPSI had vac trucks on site and were in the process of remediation (Photo 1).The spill was located around Gas Production Unit (GPU) 6H. The leak originated at the elbow joint of the associated GPU piping. The spilled fluid reached the underside of the pad liner; the fluid was also pooling on top of the pad liner, within the pea gravel (Photos 2-5).Several sumps were dug on both sides of the spill origin at GPU 6H and its associated elbow joint within the piping. Conductivity readings were obtained within the soil and water at the sump locations. The sump located 15 feet from the elbow joint yielded a conductivity reading of 1835 uS/cm within the soil (Photo 6). The sump 30 feet from the elbow joint yielded a conductivity reading of 644 uS/cm within the soil (Photo 7). The sump located 10 feet from the elbow yielded a water conductivity reading of 13.04 mS/cm and a soil reading of 6.18 mS/cm (Photos 8, 9). The sump located 35 feet from the elbow yielded a conductivity reading of 2.86 mS/cm within the soil this reading was unable to be replicated; the operator will monitor this location (Photo 10). The sump located 20 feet from the elbow yielded a conductivity reading of 176.2 uS/cm within the water, and a reading of 2.83 mS/cm within the soil (Photos 11, 12).The large sump, to the left of GPU 6H, yielded a conductivity reading of 1660 uS/cm within the water, and a reading of 2.48 mS/cm within the soil (Photos 13-15). The large sump, to the right of GPU 6H, yielded a conductivity reading of 397 uS/cm within the water, and a reading of 8.26 mS/cm within the soil (Photos 16-18).The soil within the impacted area yielded a reading of 13.39 mS/cm (Photo 19). The water on the liner yielded a conductivity reading that was Over Range (>20.00 mS/cm) (Photo 20).The soil adjacent to the sump behind GPU 6H yielded a conductivity reading of 670 uS/cm; the soil within the sump yielded a reading of 7.55 mS/cm, and the water within this sump yielded a reading of 1450 uS/cm (Photos 21-23).The pooled water and soil on the far side of the berm, behind GPU 6H, did not display elevated conductivity (Photo 24).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan was on site. A QR code was available and displayed a large list of materials located on well sites. The information did not appear to be site specific (Photo 25).Due to the release of production fluid, violations of 78a54, SWMA 301, 78a57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Comments: Incident inspection of Expand's "Lucy" Marcellus well site.Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP on September 18, 2025 (yesterday) to report an unknown quantity of brine released onto the pad surface that they discovered the same day.I met with Steve Moyer on site. Expand finished hydraulically fracturing the 6 new Marcellus wells at this site. He explained that while washing wooden mats yesterday on top of plastic liner they discovered a hole in the liner which leaked some of the wash water onto the pad surface. After removing the liner a vac truck removed pooled liquid from the pad surface. Then an excavator that was already on site to grade the pad removed the moist pad material in the approximately 50'x160' area and 1-2" deep. That material is now staged on felt and plastic liners and covered with plastic liner on the NW corner of the pad. Expand completed the cleanup the same day of the release. Crescent Environmental directed the cleanup and field verified it by testing electrical conductivity (EC) of the pad material. The impacted pad material had EC of 5-6 mS/cm. They also collected confirmatory samples of the material after the cleanup was complete. Chesapeake spudded 6 conductor casings here on October 9, 2024. Precision 569 ST-1500 drilled the 6 new Marcellus wells here December 17, 2024 thru late February 2025.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface. Moist pad material has electrical conductivity of 0.28 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test probe.Air temp 69FJLP

Comments: On November 2 2023, the Department conducted an inspection of the Keeno 2 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the well head leaking fluid. Accompanying in today's inspection was Curtis Small (Pa DEP OGI).At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled. However, the well did not appear to be equipped for production. The production line from the well did not appear to be connected to a production unit or other visual production apparatus. The pump jack did not appear to be operational.The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, fluid was observed emanating from the well head in the location of the plunger rod. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.04 mS. Conductivity readings of the fluid were taken and they indicated elevated levels of contaminants with direct reading of the water of 0.30mS and soil readings of 0.15mS and 0.11mS. Elevated readings were detected in about a 2 foot radius around the well head. No distressed vegetation was observed and no waters of the Commonwealth appeared to have been affected by this release. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted Apollo Resources Representative Jame Stiffler to inform him of the release. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to correct the condition creating the release and remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy. Mr. Stiffler indicated that they would sent someone out to correct the leak, and remediate the area as needed. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid and/or other fluids resulting in a release to the ground. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity of fluid released and how this was determined, and how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.

Comments: An onsite inspection of the Kennedy 4 well was conducted by OGI Pat Hiles. Present during the inspection was Diversified representative Gary Molek and Moody and Associates, Inc. representative Jon Hafer. The Department screened around the 7" casing upon arrival with a Bascom Turner 611. Gas readings of 19%, 6%, and 32% gas was detected at various points surrounding the casing. After further investigation, it appeared that Diversified had poured cement around the exposed 7" casing. Placing cement around the casing does not meet repair standards of 78.86. Once Mr. Molek and Mr. Hafer arrived on location, a commingle pressure of the production casing, tubing, and annulus was garnered using a digital pressure gauge. The commingle pressure recorded was 0.6 psi and this location was used as a sample point by Moody. The wellhead was then reconfigured to conduct an annulus shut in test. At 11:51 the annulus pressure was 0.5 psi before blowing the well down. At 11:55 the annulus pressure was 0.9 psi and the casing blown down. At 12:40 the annulus was at 2.0 psi and blown down to collect a sample. Although pressure was relatively low, there was decent volume. The area surrounding the wellhead was screened for soil gas at intervals of 2 ft, 10 ft, and 20 ft. Soil gas readings from Moody and the Department will be listed below. Landowner has a water well approximately 200 ft from the wellhead. The landowner stated his water well is drilled to a depth of 200 ft. Landowner's water was field screened by Moody and the results were 2% LEL, 2880 ppm, and 5220 ppm. The landowner's basement headspace and water well connections were also screened by Moody with no gas readings detected. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/30/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 1000296
Permit API: 081-21944
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/30/2023
Comments: A routine inspection was conducted in order to assess overall site conditions. A Precision Drilling rig is still in operation on the well pad. I first looked at the trench along the side of the well site secondary containment. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the trench was 764 uS/cm. A sheen was observed on the surface near the ramp over for the backyard area which appeared consistent with an iron-reducing bacteria sheen. Company man Pat Smith walked over to me while I was looking at the trench and told me that there had just been a release of a base oil to the pad surface next to the upright base oil tanks. We walked over to the base oil tanks and I saw an area of fluid on the pad surface immediately adjacent to the secondary containment for the base oil tanks. The area was approximately 30 ft by 10 ft. Mr. Smith said that the estimated volume of the release was 20 gallons. The electrical conductivity of the fluid was 1.0 uS/cm as measured by the Oakton conductivity meter. Mr. Smith said that Tobias Excavation was on the way to scrape up the impacted pad material. On July 2, 2023 EQT representative Rick Hall sent an email to the Department which included a document which detailed the remediation of the base oil release. The report included the volume of material excavated, 8 tons, the dimensions of the pad that was scraped, 20 ft wide by 40 ft long by 6 ft deep, as well as photos of the area during excavation and after the area was backfilled with new gravel. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Gabonay National City Bank 6 well in response to the operator's submission of a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well. This inspection is being separated into 3 inspection reports due to the number of photos taken. The narrative of all 3 inspection reports are identical except for the references to photos. This is inspection report 1 of 3.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced. E and S plan is present on-site at the mailbox at the beginning of the access road.Well is tagged and posted. Production tank is observed within an adequately vegetated berm at this time. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at this time. The RCE is not installed as depicted on the plans. Minimal gravel is observed, which appears to be pre-existing. The access road does not appear to be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plans calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary." Four locations on the access road are experiencing erosion and sedimentation off of the access road (Photos 10-13, 18). CFS is also not observed in these locations despite the E and S plan call for CFS installed "as needed."There are 8 culvert crossings observed during today's inspection. Some ends of the culverts are blocked due to what appears to be recent soil and vegetation clearing off the access road. Some of the culvert crossings appear to possibly be stream crossings. A follow up inspection is being requested with Department Biologists to identify possible streams and/or wetlands. CFS is not observed to be installed at any of the culvert crossings except for the last culvert crossing closest to the site. The CFS at this crossing appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time, but is only installed on one side of the crossing. The E and S plans on site do not delineate or identify any stream or wetlands or crossings of any streams or wetlands, and no 105 permits are observed on site or at any of the crossings at this time. The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.CFS is observed to be installed on-site near the well and appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time. The location of the CFS appears to be placed in the correct area in relation to the site's topography, however the E and S plans depict the CFS to be placed on the opposite (East) side of the site. A small channel of stormwater appears to be leaving the site and passing through CFS at this time, however no sediment is observed leaving the site. The Department recommends the operator monitor and maintain this area as necessary to ensure CFS continues to function properly. Plastic matting is observed to be installed in 3 locations along the access road.The Department recommends the operator redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.Violations are being issued for accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending consultation with Department Biologists.

Comments: Evidence of stressed and dead vegetation in the vicinity of the Akins lease tank battery was visible from Rounds Hill Road. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection. This inspection was conducted to document findings of an apparent release of production fluids from the Akins tank battery, as well as a separate release from a brine tank previously removed from the nearby Loomis lease's tank battery. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners previously indicated that he had checked and found the integrity of the Loomis lease brine tank to be sufficient for future use. Kyle indicated that the tank was empty and would be unused until repurposed.The PVC drain line within the secondary containment area of the Akins tank battery was found to be improperly placed. The PVC line straddles the cutout hole in the surface of the brine tank in such a manner that fluids draining through the line would be able to flow over the surface of the brine tank and pool within the secondary containment area. Soil within secondary containment immediately below the PVC line was found to have specific conductance in excess of 17,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Evidence of pooling was visible in the containment area via crude oil staining and stressed vegetation. This indicates that fluid once filled the secondary containment, but apparently was able to migrate downward and/or outward through the secondary containment diking. Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/31/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 997050
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/31/2023
Comments: Site inspection conducted at the COP Tract 551B pad to review use of EWS VOX4 evaporators for processing flowback water. Meeting on site today with EWS representative Pat Pascarella. There are no EQT personnel on site at time of inspection. A TetraTek crew is loading produced fluid into water trucks. Weather conditions are partly sunny and 73 degrees F. Wind is blowing from the southwest at an estimated 5 mph. Eight EWS Vox4 evaporators are in use at time of inspection. Evaporators process fluid in batches, with automated systems in use to pump water into the system from the production fluid tanks and out to the frac tank batteries when fluid is concentrated. All pipelines and fluid control systems appear to be functioning as designed and there is no fluid or precipitation within evaporator containment. As authorized under the Air Quality Request for Determination Operating Permit, EQT will take four evaporators out of service after the initial 60 days of use. According to Mr. Pascarella, four units will be disconnected on June 13. There are no violations associated with the evaporator authorization. Fluid with elevated conductivity (3.14 mS/cm) is still present at the NE pad sump (photo 7). Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.
